subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps for ACME
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@acme.inc>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps for ACME

Hi Sam 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our demo:

What we heard
- Primary workloads: user-facing summarization + RAG-based Q&A (latency-sensitive, p99 target ~400ms for short responses)
- Secondary: list-ranking and light personalization at scale
- SLOs: <500ms p95, maintain current output quality; cost sensitivity for high-volume endpoints

Initial recommended shortlist (tradeoffs: cost / latency / quality)
1) redwood-7b-q4f (hosted) 
— Best starting point for cost-sensitive, low-latency production. Quantized 4-bit; strong latency profile, low per-token cost. Expect good quality on summarization after a small prompt tuning pass.
2) llama-2-13b-8bit (dedicated) 
— Balanced option: higher quality on longer-form context with moderate cost. Good if you need improved coherence on multi-sentence summaries.
3) mixtral-8x7b (dedicated/private) 
— Highest quality for subtle reasoning/edge-case correctness; higher cost and longer latency (recommend for selective fallback or batch evaluation).

Why these three
- We want a fallback strategy that keeps your public endpoints low-cost and fast (redwood-7b-q4f) while giving a clear upgrade path for difficult cases (llama-13b) and a top-tier model for safety/accuracy-sensitive flows (mixtral).

Attached: prompt set we used in the demo and initial benchmark CSV. I also uploaded the full benchmark run to our drive: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026

Proposed next steps
- Your team: confirm 1–2 priority prompt sets you want us to run across the shortlist (we attached our demo set as acme-prompt-set-20260227.json).
- Redwood: run a 2k-sample eval across the three models, return latency + quality delta table and candidate guardrails for rollout.
- Optional: schedule a 30–45 minute eval planning call next week to align on success metrics (dates Fri 3/5 or Mon 3/8 currently open).

If that sounds good I’ll start the eval and loop Nikhil for config / infra details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments (sent): acme-prompt-set-20260227.json (prompt set stub), acme-benchmark-results-20260227.csv (initial sample)

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps for ACME — engineering notes

Team — forwarding Sam’s questions and adding recommended eval/config notes below. Please keep internal.

Key answers and config suggestions:
- Expected latency (hosted, us-west) for ~300 token response:
  * redwood-7b-q4f: p95 ~120–180ms, p99 ~270–380ms (continuous batching on our serving runtime; depends on concurrency)
  * llama-2-13b-8bit: p95 ~240–320ms, p99 ~500ms+ (dedicated capacity; better quality but higher variance on p99)
  * mixtral-8x7b: p95 ~350–500ms, p99 700ms+ (recommend for async/batch or selective fallback)

- Cost (ballpark per 1M tokens):
  * redwood-7b-q4f: $60–$120 / 1M tokens (quantized path, optimized kernels)
  * llama-2-13b-8bit: $180–$320 / 1M tokens
  * mixtral-8x7b: $350–$900 / 1M tokens (size and allocation dependent)

Evaluation plan (2k prompts):
- Run canonical 2k sample across the three models with the attached prompt set. Capture: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), ROUGE/L, BLEU where applicable, and a human spot-check for hallucination rate on a 200-sample subset.
- Define regression threshold: any model that drops >3% relative ROUGE-L vs your current baseline or shows >5% increase in hallucination rate will be flagged for further prompt tuning before rollout.
- Recommend staged rollout: start public traffic on redwood-7b-q4f + shadow traffic to llama-13b; route complex queries to llama/mixtral via heuristics or a classifier if quality issues arise.

Attachments: acme-benchmark-results-20260227.csv (initial demo run), acme-prompt-set-20260227.json

Nikhil / Monica — can you spin up the eval job (hosted + dedicated where needed) and share the run-id / results link? Add any infra caveats (e.g., dedicated capacity lead time) in your reply.

Thanks,
Marissa

Following up with the consolidated shortlist and artifacts (attached). Quick summary so your procurement and engineering teams have the right context: 

Shortlist summary:
- redwood-7b-q4f (recommended pilot): low-latency, low-cost, good quality for summarization after prompt tuning. Good for immediate rollout and A/B testing.
- llama-2-13b-8bit (upgrade path): moderate cost, better long-form coherence; recommended as shadow or canary for complex queries.
- mixtral-8x7b (selective fallback): highest accuracy for edge cases; use selectively where correctness is critical.

Deliverables attached: acme-prompt-set-20260227.json, acme-benchmark-results-20260227.csv, acme-model-shortlist-v1.pdf (one-pager with tradeoffs and recommended rollout).

— happy to loop legal.
